text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Finland's Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen told visiting Nato Secretary-General Javier Solana that Finland is interested in broad cooperation with NATO as a whole and does not want to be tied down to limited cooperation in the Baltic region.
- Musical show to be staged this week at Linnanmaki amusement park in memory of rock-and-roll legend Elvis Presely. Elvis' widow Priscilla and daughter Lisa Marie will attend. @

- Relations between late president Urho Kekkonen and Mauno Koivisto almost broke down during Koivisto's term as prime minister (1968-1970) because Kekkonen disliked Koivisto's independence, new book says.
- Finnish nature conservation project to receive 30 million markka funding from the EU as part of the European Natura 2000 network.
- A planned forestry project under Finland's development cooperation with Nepal raises controversies with local non-governmental organisations. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finland's social transfer payments to working-age population growing despite cuts in benefits. Annual transfers have grown by 34 billion markka since 1990.
- Morgan Stanley says it is not time to buy forestry shares, as newsprint and fine paper prices still declining.
- Foreign investors now own one sixth of wholesale and retail group Kesko.
- Unemployment among Swedish-speaking Finns 9.2 percent vs 15.7 percent for the population as a whole. @
DEMARI
- MP Erikki Tuomioja seen as favourite to succeed Pertti Paasio as leader of the Social Democratic parliamentary group once Paasio goes to the European Parliament.
- Farmers' earnings fell by 15 percent on average after Finland joined the European Union.
AAMULEHTI
- Hunters shot 73 bears this season, which ended on October 15. Some say the hunting season should be extended by a month.
- Live moths found in red and yellow Spanish peppers. @
- UPM-Kymmene ready to buy more timber than land owners willing to sell -- tries ad campaign to attract sellers.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Almost 600 people queued last week in Turku for Salvation Army food packages. Situation worse than ever, aid worker said.
- Left-Wing Alliance deputy chairwoman Suvi-Anne Siimes ready to consider changing the party's cabinet ministers.
